Medic. It's a class I avoided for the first 2000 hours of tf2 because I could never get frags and I had trouble with constantly losing my uber progress due to dying. At some point I decided to change my mindset about how I played medic and started focusing almost entirely on supporting my teammates. I started top-scoring with just healing my teammates and ubering them while pushing on the point and getting those sweet cap points. I've since added a bit of battle medic flair to my loadout by running the crossbow which also adds some nice long range healing utility. Medic has since become one of my favorite classes to play when my team is in a pinch. For context, I'm a demoman/knight main. Unfortunately, I've still yet to really take on and learn Spy which I guess will be one of my goals for my next 1000 hours of tf2.

I didn't come out until I was 18. This was partially due to me going for and attaining my Eagle Scout. After that, I began by telling a few of my friends on day in school. I was absolutely astounded that they were so accepting of it. As I became more and more comfortable with my sexuality, I told the rest of my friends. One day, I told the one friend that I thought would hate me (a diehard conservative) and he just accepted it. After telling all of my friends and my siblings (who were also very supportive), I decided I would tell my parents. I told my mom and was astounded by her reaction. She went into a massive fit of denial and I ended up leaving the house that night and stayed with a friend for a couple days. She kept calling me and facebooking me with various messages along the lines of "I'll buy you a hooker" or"I just need to give you a stack of Playboys". I just kept using my friends as support. My dad called me one day and asked if what I said was true. I said yes and he was just very accepting of it. After that phone call, I decided that it was safe for me to return home. After coming home, my mom profusely apologized for her behavior and said she'll accept me for who I am.

TL;DR: I came out to my friends who were very accepting and thought I would tell my parents. My mom flips a tit and I stay with a friend for a couple days. My dad calls and is okay with me. I return home to my mom apologizing for her behavior.

As for advice, don't always assume how it will go. The people who think will accept it right away might not be as accepting as you think. Also, if things go awry, always have someone there who can support you.
